episode_title: Ep. 260: Thy Distillery with Jakob Stjernholm

real_qa.q: What is Thy Distillery's approach to grain selection and terroir in whiskey production?
real_qa.r: Thy Distillery sources approximately 30 old barley varieties from the Nordic Gene Bank and has narrowed production to three primary varieties: Imperial, which brings citrus and lemony flavors with oily mouthfeel; Langeland, which offers earthy and orange citrus notes; and a modern variety providing sweet, malty flavors. Jakob Stjernholm emphasizes that barley variety selection is massively more important than the exact location of the field in creating distinct flavor profiles, comparing it to how different grape varieties create different wines.
real_qa.requete: Thy Distillery barley varieties flavor differences

real_qa.q: How does Thy Distillery obtain ancient barley varieties from the Nordic Gene Bank for whiskey production?
real_qa.r: The Nordic Gene Bank holds thousands of barley varieties collected over the last 150 years, with original storage in Svalbard, a remote island north of Norway kept at freezing temperatures. Farmers receive only small amounts—what can be held in one's hands—and must hand-sow and hand-harvest these seeds for the first couple of years until reaching enough volume to use farming equipment. It takes six to seven years from initial seed to harvesting 30 tons or more of mature barley that can be used for full-scale whiskey production.
real_qa.requete: Nordic Gene Bank ancient barley varieties how obtain

real_qa.q: What is the seven-year crop rotation system used at Thy Distillery's 500-hectare farm?
real_qa.r: Thy Distillery employs organic farming with a seven-year crop rotation designed for both weed management and soil nutrient replenishment. A typical rotation includes two years of clover and grass for grazing (which fixes nitrogen), followed by barley in the second year after grass when nutrition levels are optimal, then wheat or spelt consuming excess nitrogen, rye as a robust low-nitrogen crop, and finally legumes or broad beans before returning to grass. This rotation prevents pest buildup from consecutive identical crops and maintains soil organic matter without artificial fertilizers.
real_qa.requete: seven year crop rotation organic farming barley

real_qa.q: Why did Thy Distillery need to design and build custom malting equipment instead of using existing facilities?
real_qa.r: Existing malting factories in Denmark, such as the local facility in Tissel, process massive batches of 250 tons at a time, making them unsuitable for small craft distillery volumes. When Thy Distillery attempted to malt one to four tons of heritage barley varieties, the commercial malting factory could not accommodate such small batches, forcing the farm to develop its own in-house malting system between 2015-2016 and 2019.
real_qa.requete: Thy Distillery custom malting equipment why needed

real_qa.q: What awards has Thy Distillery received for its single estate and heritage grain whiskeys?
real_qa.r: Thy Distillery won the World Whiskey Awards at the London World Whiskey Awards for best single estate distillery and for best wheat whiskey, a smaller category in which they produce whiskey from spelt, emmer, and Oeland nordic wheat varieties.

guest.titre: Co-owner, Master Distiller, and Managing Director
guest.bio_context: Jakob Stjernholm is the co-owner, master distiller, and managing director of Thy Distillery in Denmark, a farm distillery based on his family's farm with eight generations of farming history dating back to 1773. He and his family took over the farm in the seventh generation and began building their distillery from 2015-2016, launching full-scale operations in 2019. Thy Distillery operates as a single estate distillery where every step of whiskey production—from organic farming to malting, distilling, maturing, and bottling—occurs on the same site.

real_quote: We are a farm distillery and a single estate distillery meaning that we do every single step of the process of making whiskey from farming organically in our own fields, malting, distilling, maturing, bottling—so everything is done at one site.
